======================================================================
  Step 8  Expected-cost threshold analysis
======================================================================
  Cost model:
    E(thr) = P(D)*FNR(thr)*C_miss + (1-P(D))*FPR(thr)*C_fa,
    with C_fa normalised to 1 and C_miss = 20.
  Why the asymmetry is justified:
    A false alarm costs ONE manual re-inspection: an inspector already on
    site taps the flagged point again. A miss is a potential
    FALLING-OBJECT SAFETY EVENT: a debonded finish that is never
    re-inspected can detach and fall from height onto the public below.
    The ratio therefore prices the consequences, not the inspection effort.
  reference classifier : Logistic regression
  assumed prior P(D)   : 0.15
  theoretical thr      : 1/(1+m) = 0.0476 (for a perfectly calibrated model)
  COST-OPTIMAL thr     : 0.2226  ->  expected cost 0.48000 per tap
    at that threshold  : FNR = 0.0750 (missed debonds), FPR = 0.3000 (needless re-inspections)
  naive default thr    : 0.5000  ->  expected cost 0.62111 per tap
    at that threshold  : FNR = 0.1850, FPR = 0.0778
  saving from choosing the optimum: 0.14111 per tap (22.7% of the default cost)
  degenerate strategies: never alarm = 3.00000, always alarm = 0.85000
